records.f: UK fixed voice service revenues totalled £891.9 million in Q1 2026, down £49.5 million or 5.3% quarter on quarter and £194.2 million or 17.9% year on year.
records.g: National revenue trends do not establish broadband availability, speed or service quality at a particular premises.

records.f: The total number of UK fixed lines fell by 757,000 or 3.5% during Q1 2026 to 20.7 million.
records.g: A national fixed-line count does not identify the access technology or connection status of an individual address.

records.f: UK fixed-originated call volumes decreased by 583 million minutes or 14.9% year on year to 3.32 billion minutes in Q1 2026.
records.g: Aggregate call volumes are market activity data and provide no exact-address connectivity evidence.

records.f: Mobile telephony services generated £3.57 billion in retail revenues in Q1 2026, £55.6 million or 1.6% higher than a year earlier.
records.g: National mobile revenue does not establish coverage, capacity or service quality at a parcel.

records.f: Average monthly mobile retail revenue per subscriber was £13.10 in Q1 2026; post-pay averaged £15.54 and pre-pay £5.40.
records.g: Subscriber revenue averages do not prove local coverage, achievable speed or address-level eligibility.

records.f: Mobile-originated voice call minutes declined by 1.76 billion or 4.6% year on year to 36.34 billion minutes; calls to landlines fell 7.2% to 6.07 billion minutes.
records.g: Traffic volumes do not measure signal strength, indoor coverage or service availability at an exact premises.

records.f: UK mobile messages including SMS and MMS fell by 1.25 billion or 21.3% year on year to 4.61 billion in Q1 2026.
records.g: National messaging volumes do not establish network reach or quality at an individual address.

records.f: Broadband complaints to Ofcom fell from a peak of 40 per 100,000 customers in 2011 to an all-time low of six per 100,000 in Q1 2026.
records.g: Complaint rates concern major providers and reported dissatisfaction; they do not prove availability or quality at a specific address.

records.f: Compared with Q4 2025, Q1 2026 complaints about fixed broadband and pay-monthly mobile decreased, while landline and pay-TV complaint levels stayed the same.
records.g: Quarterly complaint direction is a sector-level quality indicator and does not establish exact-premises service conditions.

records.f: Ofcom identified TalkTalk as the most complained-about fixed broadband provider in Q1 2026, while Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed broadband complaints.
records.g: Provider complaint rankings do not establish network availability, line performance or suitability for a specific parcel.
